title: Quantum Geometry in Hyperbolic Band Theory
authors: Ahmed Adel Mahmoud, Riccardo Sorbello, Ronny Thomale, Steven Rayan
abstract: Hyperbolic band theory (HBT) has recently unveiled a wealth of exotic physical phenomena in negatively curved spaces. Concurrently, the quantum metric has emerged as a fundamental tensor governing quantum geometry and topological phases. In this Letter, we bridge these two frontiers by investigating the quantum metric in HBT. Because conventional Euclidean metric extraction protocols fundamentally fail in these non-commutative geometries, we introduce holonomy shaking, a novel, experimentally viable technique utilizing periodic lattice driving to dynamically extract the metric. Using the {8,3} regular hyperbolic and kagome-like lattices as concrete examples, we demonstrate the high-fidelity dynamical extraction of the quantum metric. Our results establish a robust blueprint for probing hyperbolic quantum geometries, paving the way for the discovery of exotic topological phenomena in hyperbolic quantum matter.
summary: This paper develops a novel technique called 'holonomy shaking' to measure the quantum metric in systems governed by hyperbolic band theory. By using periodic lattice driving, the authors overcome theoretical hurdles associated with non-commutative hyperbolic geometries. This provides a powerful, experimentally actionable method for characterizing exotic topological phases in hyperbolic quantum matter.
main_problem: The paper aims to bridge the study of hyperbolic band theory (HBT) with the quantum metric, addressing the failure of conventional Euclidean metric extraction protocols in non-commutative hyperbolic geometries.
main_result: The authors introduce 'holonomy shaking,' a novel dynamical protocol that successfully extracts the quantum metric for hyperbolic lattices, providing a blueprint for probing hyperbolic quantum matter.
method: The core method is 'holonomy shaking,' which uses periodic lattice driving (time-periodic harmonic drive) to modulate Aharonov-Bohm phases and track resulting excitation rates to calculate the quantum metric.
model_or_system: The system involves quantum particles on hyperbolic lattices, specifically using $\{8, 3\}$ regular hyperbolic and kagome-like lattices. The theory is formulated using the Abelian sector of HBT, parameterized by the flat Jacobian torus.

The primary observable is the Quantum Metric ($g_{\mu

important_parameters: The analysis is performed in the Abelian U(1) sector, utilizing parameters related to the Aharonov-Bohm phases ($k_j$) and the driving frequency ($\omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the Abelian U(1) sector, which is assumed to be an exact, algebraically closed subset of states, simplifying the quantum geometric tensor calculation.

paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework of HBT and the quantum metric. It then details the failure of standard protocols, leading to the introduction of the novel 'holonomy shaking' technique. The method is applied to specific hyperbolic lattices, demonstrating the extraction of the metric components.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics as it proposes an experimentally viable, dynamic spectroscopic technique (lattice driving) to probe fundamental geometric properties (quantum metric) in engineered quantum systems, analogous to how cold atoms or superconducting circuits can realize synthetic gauge fields.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) The octagonal fundamental domain used for the {8, 3} hyperbolic lattice. The colored arrows denote the non- contractible generators of the Fuchsian translation group Γ, mapping opposite edges to establish periodic boundary con- ditions. (b) The Bloch spectrum and the isolated lowest-band quantum metric along the trajectory k = (k1, π, π, π). At the high-symmetry torsion point k1 = π, the bands touch, causing the rank-one quantum metric to develop a sharp singularity.

FIG. 2. Kinematic extraction of the diagonal quantum metric components in the hyperbolic Abelian momentum space. (a) The energy spectrum and the highly accurate extraction of g11 (red circles) against the exact analytical formula (solid black line) along k1 ∈[0, 2π] with k2 = π, k3 = k4 = π/2. (b) The corresponding spectrum and precision extraction for the g33 component along k3 ∈[0, 2π] with k1 = k2 = π, k4 = π/2.

(a) Spectrum of the regular hyperbolic {8, 3} lattice and its Abelian metric component g11, comparing the ideal values (black crosses) with those extracted through holonomy shaking (orange circles). (b) Logarithmic spatial map of the absolute extraction error |gext 11 −gideal 11 | on the underlying lattice with one metric value assigned to each unit cell. (c) Spectrum of the {8, 3} Kagome-like lattice, prominently exhibiting an eightfold- degenerate flat ground-state band, together with the extracted trace Tr g11 of its non-Abelian quantum metric.
